body: @callebtc happy to adjust anything here if it helps for the release.
Closing: upstream formatCurrency now has the same try/catch fallback, so this is covered.
Trimmed to the one-line change and rebased on main.

Note for reviewers: the Oct 11–12 red X's on every workflow are `No jobs were run` startup failures — a GitHub Actions glitch that also hit other PRs opened in that window (#620 failed identically), not a problem with this change; the code has never actually been through CI. Updated the branch with main so the workflows re-trigger fresh against the current tree.

Hi!I 

looked into this more and couldn’t reproduce the comma-separated numbers in the real app (Chromium, dev + production builds). The old toString() already returns the correct token because the browser gets a Buffer.

The first version of the PR broke CBOR text strings (scan stayed stuck). The updated code now handles string, Buffer, and Uint8Array so that doesn’t happen.

For what cashu.me actually sends, the result is the same as before.

Happy to keep it as hardening or close it.

Thanks for checking the real browser path and catching the text-string regression. My earlier comment overstated the current impact: if the decoder returns a Buffer in the app, its existing `toString()` produces the token rather than comma-separated bytes. The updated diff handles strings and byte arrays, though I don't see an automated regression for those forms. Whether the additional hardening is worthwhile is a maintainer decision. I reviewed the diff but did not run tests locally. AI-assisted review.

Thanks for adding coverage. I rechecked head `75add81`: the new component test exercises the completed-scan callback with mocked `decodeCBOR()` results for a string, Buffer, and plain Uint8Array, and checks the emitted token. That covers the byte-to-text behavior I raised; the decoder itself is mocked, so it is not a CBOR round-trip test. I reviewed the patch but did not run it locally. AI-assisted review.
Thanks calle. Your comments made me rethink the approach. The dialog now keeps the unit of the shown request, offers the units of that request's mint, and leaves the wallet's unit alone.
